problem: Bounded prime gaps via smooth moduli (Zhang 2013)

board.name: the GPY sieve, UNCHANGED
board.S: Selberg sieve weights lambda_d, one-variable F -- exactly GPY's
board.I: the same ratio criterion, still capped at 2*theta

what_happened: Zhang works WITHIN GPY. He does not touch the sieve; he improves its INPUT, raising the effective level of distribution past 1/2 for smooth moduli: Theorem 3.2, y-smooth moduli, Q = x^{1/2+eta}, eta/2 = delta = 1/1168. Granville sec. 5 asks whether GPY survives Zhang's restrictions -- i.e. Zhang is measured against an unchanged GPY board.
tests_for: False board-change alarms, and uniquely: it is CONTEMPORANEOUS with a real board change on the SAME problem at the same stakes (case 7a). Every other positive/control comparison in P1 is cross-problem and confounded by difficulty. This one is not.

level_flag.warning: ZHANG IS NOT SIMPLY BETTER PLAY, and calling him that would mislabel this control.
level_flag.what_he_did: He changed the EQUIDISTRIBUTION board one level down -- smooth moduli, factored modulus, Graham-Ringrose. So 7b is a LEVEL-(n-1) BOARD CHANGE feeding an UNCHANGED LEVEL-n board.
level_flag.consequence: This is a THIRD CATEGORY the five-transformation catalogue never had and the rebuilt diagnostic does not express. The control is valid only with the level stated: at level n (the sieve) the board did not change, which is what a diagnostic reading the sieve board must not fire on. At level n-1 it did.
